Authentication and camera settings

Computer: receive up to G64 · G32 controls

Choose Computer or Phone independently of its authentication role. Computer screens can send up to G128; phone screens up to G64. Choose a smaller outgoing grid when alignment is difficult. Choose one verifier and one key holder. Start both devices with 32 repetitions. Short proofs are for development; increasing repetitions increases proof size and work. Sampling and processing may take longer than the selected intervals.

The trained neural corrector will be checked when you start.

Camera exposure & focus

For glare, try a small negative exposure compensation if available. These controls change camera acquisition; no brightness filter is applied to captured pixels. Manual exposure and focus values become available after the camera confirms Manual mode.

When a G32 ACK appears, turn the phone so the sender can read it. Orange marks uncertain geometry, size or phase; green means acquisition cues passed. Only an RS+CRC-valid packet advances the exchange. Keep the ACK visible until the sender confirms delivery.

You can reduce the grid between outgoing messages. To change a stalled message, stop and restart both devices with the smaller grid.
